{'translation': '9to5Mac is presented by CleanMyMac from MacPaw. With the release of macOS 27 Golden Gate, use CleanMyMac first to free up space and optimise your system, ensuring your new Mac runs at 100% performance from day one. Learn more.'}

{'translation': "macOS 27 Golden Gate is a major upgrade over macOS 26 Tahoe, and it's not just about smarter design decisions. Just like iOS 27 on the iPhone, the Mac now gets a Liquid Glass appearance slider. Users can use it to dramatically change the look of the entire Mac interface."}

{'translation': 'Slider'}

{'translation': "Liquid Glass is Apple's design language, first introduced with iOS 26 and macOS 26 Tahoe. Liquid Glass initially came in only one look, but Apple later added a setting option to make Liquid Glass less transparent."}

{'translation': 'Starting with iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate, Liquid Glass is no longer limited to just two styles. Apple has introduced an appearance slider that can make Liquid Glass more transparent than before. It can also make it more opaque, while still maintaining a modern look.'}

{'translation': 'macOS 27 Golden Gate defaults to the medium setting. The system will also invite you to adjust the slider during the initial setup process. You can readjust the slider later in System Settings > Appearance.'}

{'translation': 'The Liquid Glass slider provides a real-time preview for each setting. The three marks represent most transparent, medium, and most opaque. Of course, you can also set the slider anywhere between the marks.'}

{'translation': 'The Dock'}

{'translation': 'The Dock is the most prominent component that changes its appearance based on the Liquid Glass slider setting.'}

{'translation': 'Its range can go from clearly showing your desktop wallpaper, to becoming a more opaque, more substantial material.'}

{'translation': "Here's a closer look at the effect:"}

{'translation': 'Widgets'}

{'translation': 'macOS desktop widgets can be full-colour, dimmed, or automatic. The Liquid Glass slider also changes the appearance of dimmed widgets.'}

{'translation': 'Apple Music and Podcasts'}

{'translation': 'Apps with system Now Playing controls, such as Apple Music and Podcasts, will look dramatically different depending on where the Liquid Glass slider is set.'}

{'translation': "Here's an example using the Podcasts Now Playing controls:"}

{'translation': "And here's the effect in Music:"}

{'translation': 'More'}

{'translation': 'The slider also applies to sidebars, toolbars, and toolbar buttons. The appearance of Photos, Safari, and other apps with window interface elements will also change accordingly.'}

{'translation': "There's one thing to note about the Liquid Glass slider in macOS 27 Golden Gate: a single slider controls the Liquid Glass appearance across the entire system. That means the Dock, widgets, and window interface elements will all share a unified style."}

{'translation': "Which one do you prefer? More transparent, more opaque, or in between? Personally, I really love the mature, refined look of the more opaque option on my Mac. Of course, trying out the more transparent effect is also fun, and I'm glad macOS 27 Golden Gate gives everyone the freedom to choose."}

{'translation': 'Share your thoughts in the comments section!'}
